investigation.title: local-agent-runtime eval failure: upstream model provider returned 424 provider_account_unavailable, blocking all required evidence collection
investigation.summary: The local-agent-runtime eval check failed because POST /api/agents/[REDACTED]/runtime/test returned HTTP 502, wrapping an upstream 424 Failed Dependency with error code provider_account_unavailable. Because the LLM call never completed, the probe collected zero evidence fields (orgId, agentId, model, provider, message all missing), causing a total contract validation failure against the expected-output contract defined in infra/evals/status/check-expectations.json lines 102–105.
investigation.rootCause: The AURA backend was temporarily unable to reach the configured model provider at the time of the eval run (2026-10-08T02:31:15–23Z). The provider gateway returned HTTP 424 with code provider_account_unavailable, which the harness surfaced as an llm_error and propagated as a 502 bad_gateway to the eval runner. Because the runtime test call failed before any LLM response was produced, the probe returned an empty evidence object, violating all five required evidence fields and the message assertion ("hello from aura") defined in the expected-output contract. This is an eval infrastructure failure caused by a transient or sustained upstream provider connectivity issue; no evidence of a user-traffic or production incident is present in the packet.
proof: failed-check.message: POST /api/agents/[REDACTED]/runtime/test returned 502 with nested error code provider_account_unavailable and message 'AURA is temporarily unable to reach the model provider. This is an issue on our side, not with your account or credits.'
failed-check.evidence: evidence object is empty ({}); all five required fields orgId, agentId, model, provider, message are absent.
expected-output.missing-required-evidence: contract gap lists all five required evidence keys as missing: orgId, agentId, model, provider, message.

expected-output.contract (infra/evals/status/check-expectations.json lines 102–105): requiredEvidence=[orgId, agentId, model, provider, message] and assertion message containsIgnoreCase 'hello from aura' — none satisfied.

sibling.local-agent-create (status=pass, latencyMs=5885): agent creation succeeded and returned agentId, orgId, machineType, environment — confirming the agent lifecycle layer is healthy and the failure is isolated to the LLM runtime call.
sibling.local-agent-permissions (status=pass, latencyMs=5641): permissions bundle was persisted successfully — further confirming the failure is not a shared auth or org-resolution dependency.

failed-check.timing: latencyMs=7408, well within the warningLatencyMs=15000 and outageLatencyMs=45000 thresholds defined in infra/evals/status/features.json line 81 — the failure is not a timeout; it is an explicit upstream error response.
possibleCauses: Most likely: Transient provider-side outage or rate-limit event at the time of the scheduled eval run (2026-10-08T02:31Z), causing the model provider gateway to return 424 provider_account_unavailable. The error message explicitly states this is not an account or credits issue.

Less likely but possible: A sustained or recurring provider connectivity degradation affecting the specific model or provider configured for the local-agent-runtime harness test, which would cause repeated failures on subsequent runs.

Less likely: A misconfiguration of the provider account credentials or model routing in the eval harness environment (desktop-nightly-macos-aarch64 / desktop-release), though the error message text and provider_account_unavailable code point to a server-side provider reachability issue rather than a credential problem.

Least likely given sibling pass results: A shared dependency failure (auth, org resolution, agent creation) — ruled out because local-agent-create and local-agent-permissions both passed in the same run window.

investigation.title: Project Agent Chat Stream Eval Failure: Model Provider Unavailable (HTTP 424) Blocks Session Persistence and All Project-Agent-Workflows Checks
investigation.summary: The desktop-release eval for project-agent-chat-stream failed at 2026-10-08T02:31:37Z with an HTTP 424 error (code: provider_account_unavailable, support_id: 4a22df7c0886), meaning the AURA backend could not reach the upstream model provider during the eval run. Because the chat stream never produced a model response, the probe's runProjectChatTurn function could not collect sessionId, sessionCount, or expectedPhrase, causing three required evidence assertions to go unmet and the check to fail.
investigation.rootCause: The upstream model provider was unreachable from the AURA backend at the time of the eval run (2026-10-08T02:31:29–02:31:37Z). The API returned HTTP 424 Failed Dependency with error code provider_account_unavailable (support_id: 4a22df7c0886). This caused the chat stream to emit an error frame instead of text_delta frames, leaving textSample empty and preventing session persistence. As a direct consequence, sessionId, sessionCount, and expectedPhrase were never populated, violating the expected-output contract defined in infra/evals/status/check-expectations.json at line 120. This is an eval-time infrastructure dependency failure, not a confirmed user-facing production outage; no user-traffic or incident signals are present in the supplied evidence.
proof: failed-check.message: HTTP 424 with error code provider_account_unavailable and support_id=4a22df7c0886 is the primary failure signal returned by the chat stream API.
failed-check.evidence: frameTypes includes 'error' and 'message' but does NOT include 'text_delta'; textSample is empty string, confirming no model output was streamed.

expected-output.missing-required-evidence: sessionId, sessionCount, and expectedPhrase are all absent from the collected evidence, directly violating the contract at infra/evals/status/check-expectations.json line 120.

expected-output.contract: The contract asserts frameTypes must contain 'text_delta', textSample must contain 'hello from aura' (case-insensitive), sessionCount must be >= 1, and expectedPhrase must equal 'hello from aura' — all of which failed because no model response was produced.

sibling.session-share-public-read: This sibling check received the identical HTTP 424 provider_account_unavailable error (support_id: e22a50d1b755) at 02:34:30Z, confirming the provider outage persisted across multiple sequential eval probes.
sibling.project-agent-tool-roundtrip: frameTypes also contains 'error' with no tool invocations (toolNames: []), consistent with the agent receiving a provider error before it could act.

sibling.project-agent-a2a-roundtrip: frameTypes contains 'error' on both planner and reviewer streams; reviewerEventsError is 'Timed out after 120000ms waiting for expected value', consistent with the provider being unavailable throughout the ~140-second probe window.

sibling.project-agent-subagent-roundtrip: sessionSubagentError is 'Parent chat stream did not emit a child run id', and taskToolUsed/subagentSpawned are both false, again consistent with the agent never receiving a model response.

failed-check.timing: latencyMs=8459, well below the warningLatencyMs=30000 threshold, indicating the probe failed fast on an API error rather than timing out — consistent with a hard provider error response rather than a slow degradation.

source-context.infra/evals/status/run-status-probes.mjs:1816-1820: The runner calls runProjectChatTurn via withCleanup; if the chat stream returns an error frame, session persistence and evidence collection downstream of the stream would not complete.
possibleCauses: PRIMARY — Transient upstream model provider outage: The AURA backend returned provider_account_unavailable (HTTP 424) for all chat-stream-dependent checks across a ~3-minute window (02:31:29–02:34:30Z). This is the most strongly supported cause given two independent 424 errors with distinct support IDs and consistent error frames across all four sibling checks.

SECONDARY — Eval-account-specific provider quota or credential issue: Although the error message explicitly states 'This is an issue on our side, not with your account or credits,' a misconfigured or expired provider credential scoped to the eval service account cannot be fully ruled out without inspecting the backend provider configuration at the time of the run.

TERTIARY — Transient network partition between AURA backend and model provider endpoint: A brief network-level failure between AURA infrastructure and the provider could produce the same 424 response if the backend translates connectivity failures into this error code.

LOWER — runProjectChatTurn probe logic does not handle provider errors gracefully enough to collect partial evidence: The probe emits an error frame but still fails to populate sessionId/sessionCount/expectedPhrase; if error-path evidence collection were improved, the failure mode would be more precisely diagnosed in future runs. This does not explain the 424 itself but would affect observability.

Because the agent could not reach the model, it never produced a tool-calling turn; the stream emitted an error frame instead of assistant tool-use frames, so write_file, read_file, and run_command were never invoked and all downstream file and shell assertions failed. This is an eval-infrastructure signal of a backend provider outage scoped to the desktop-release runtime environment; no user-traffic or incident signals are present in the supplied evidence to confirm a broader production impact.

investigations.title: harness-skill-invocation: Installed skill not surfaced in agent context during real chat turn (skillInContext=false, textMatches=false)
investigations.summary: The eval check harness-skill-invocation failed because the installed skill was not present in the agent's context during the real project chat turn, and the agent's response did not contain the expected probe phrase "AURA_SKILL_PROBE_OK". Skill creation and installation both succeeded (created=true, installedOnAgent=true), but the downstream chat invocation produced an empty textSample, skillInContext=false, and textMatches=false, indicating the skill was not injected into the agent's context window or the agent did not follow it.
investigations.rootCause: The root cause is uncertain but is localized to the skill-context injection or skill-following step of the real project chat turn executed by runSkillInvocationTurn in infra/evals/status/run-status-probes.mjs. The skill was successfully created and installed on the agent (confirmed by passing sibling check harness-skills-roundtrip), but the chat stream returned an empty textSample and an error frame, indicating the agent either did not receive the skill in its context or encountered a runtime error that prevented it from producing a response containing the expected phrase. The presence of an "error" frame type in the stream is the most direct signal of a failure during the chat turn itself.

The installed skill was not injected into the agent's context window for the chat turn — the skill installation API reports success but the context-building step for the project chat session does not include the skill, possibly due to a timing issue, a missing context-assembly step, or a bug in the skill-context hydration path on desktop-release.

investigations.summary: The local-agent-runtime eval check failed because POST /api/agents/[REDACTED]/runtime/test returned HTTP 502, wrapping an upstream 424 Failed Dependency with error code provider_account_unavailable. investigations.rootCause: The AURA backend was temporarily unable to reach the configured model provider at the time of the eval run (2026-10-08T02:31:15–23Z). The provider gateway returned HTTP 424 with code provider_account_unavailable, which the harness surfaced as an llm_error and propagated as a 502 bad_gateway to the eval runner. Because the runtime test call failed before any LLM response was produced, the probe returned an empty evidence object, violating all five required evidence fields and the message assertion ("hello from aura") defined in the expected-output contract. This is an eval infrastructure failure caused by a transient or sustained upstream provider connectivity issue; no evidence of a user-traffic or production incident is present in the packet.

investigations.rootCause: The upstream model provider was unreachable from the AURA backend at the time of the eval run (2026-10-08T02:31:29–02:31:37Z). The API returned HTTP 424 Failed Dependency with error code provider_account_unavailable (support_id: 4a22df7c0886). As a direct consequence, sessionId, sessionCount, and expectedPhrase were never populated, violating the expected-output contract defined in infra/evals/status/check-expectations.json at line 120. This is an eval-time infrastructure dependency failure, not a confirmed user-facing production outage; no user-traffic or incident signals are present in the supplied evidence.

The subagent roundtrip failure is a downstream consequence of the model provider being unreachable: without a successful model completion, the `task` tool cannot be called, no child run is created, and `childRunId` is never emitted. This is an eval infrastructure signal, not confirmed user-facing production traffic impact.

whatWouldDisproveThis: A successful re-run of project-agent-chat-stream or session-share-public-read that still returns 424 after the provider reports full recovery would suggest a persistent credential or configuration problem rather than a transient outage.

A passing run of project-agent-chat-stream (textSample non-empty, sessionId present) while session-share-public-read still fails would localize the fault to the share-link generation or anonymous public-read endpoint rather than the provider.

Evidence that the 424 error is specific to the eval harness's request format (e.g., a malformed header or body introduced by a recent change) and not reproducible via a direct API call with the same credentials would implicate the runner rather than the provider.
Provider status records showing no incident during 2026-10-08T02:31–02:35Z would weaken the transient-outage hypothesis and strengthen the credential/configuration or runner-regression hypotheses.
A passing run of any project-agent-workflows sibling check during the same time window would disprove the broad provider outage hypothesis and suggest the failure is check-specific.
followUpEvals: Add a standalone provider-reachability eval that sends a minimal ping to the model provider and asserts a non-4xx response, so provider outages are surfaced as a named dependency failure rather than cascading into all project-agent-workflows checks.
Add a retry-with-backoff variant of the session-share-public-read eval that retries runProjectChatTurn once on 424 before marking the check as FAIL, to reduce noise from transient provider blips.

Add an eval that specifically exercises the anonymous public share read endpoint independently of the chat-turn prerequisite (using a pre-seeded session), so share-endpoint regressions can be distinguished from upstream provider failures.

Add a historical-baseline eval that tracks consecutive failure counts for project-agent-workflows checks and alerts when all siblings fail in the same run window, as a signal for shared dependency events.
